note: Hand-written expected answers. The pipeline is broken if it misses these. Every entry states date_precision explicitly on both the input claim and the expected verification, because precision is itself a claim: a source attesting '1985' has not attested '1985-01-01', and padding it would manufacture agreement or disagreement that no source expressed.

disputed.evidence_so_far: The event type is settled: da Vinci is absent from PMA (openfda-davinci-pma NOT_FOUND, with the PMA query proven working by openfda-pma-smoke returning 56,853 records) and has 115 510(k) records. The DATE is not settled. The earliest clearance seen is K002489, decided 2001-03-02, received 2000-08-10. Two problems with concluding anything: (1) 2000-08 is not 2000-07, so even the received date does not match the spec; (2) openfda-davinci-510k returned only 25 of 115 records in openFDA's default UNSPECIFIED order, and the oldest record is demonstrably not in that page — so an earlier clearance may exist and simply not have been retrieved.
candidate_explanations: 2000-07 refers to K002489's submission rather than its decision, misremembered by a month (received 2000-08-10).
2000-07 refers to a da Vinci clearance not present in the truncated 25-record page.
2000-07 refers to a non-FDA event entirely — a CE mark, a commercial launch, or a first clinical use.
2000-07 is simply wrong, propagated between secondary sources.

resolved_by.rule: openfda-davinci-510k-earliest sorts by decision_date ascending, so its first record IS the earliest da Vinci clearance. openfda-davinci-2000 asks directly whether any da Vinci clearance was decided in calendar 2000. If that returns NOT_FOUND, 2000-07 corresponds to no FDA decision and the date mode should be dropped to a single value with the spec date recorded as refuted. If it returns a record, anchor to it.

disputed.not_yet_changed_because: A truncated, unsorted page cannot establish an earliest date. Asserting 2001-03-02 as THE clearance date on 25 of 115 arbitrary records would repeat, in a smaller way, the error this whole exercise exists to correct.

resolved_disputes.resolved_by: openfda-pma-smoke (200, 56,853 records) and openfda-pma-syntax-control proved the PMA query path works; openfda-davinci-pma then returned NOT_FOUND, making the absence genuine; openfda-davinci-510k returned 115 matches.
resolved_disputes.note: Only the event type is resolved. The date remains disputed above.

resolved_disputes.resolved_by: Same controls: openfda-pma-smoke (200, 56,853 records) and openfda-pma-syntax-control. openfda-robodoc-pma then returned NOT_FOUND; openfda-robodoc-510k returned exactly 2 of 2 records, so unlike da Vinci this result is COMPLETE and the earliest is definitive.
resolved_disputes.note: Fully resolved: event type and date both.

deviations_from_spec.why: The primary record settles it. K931783 was received 1993-04-09 and decided 1993-11-22 — both within 1993, so there is no bimodal distribution to detect. The spec's expectation encoded the secondary-source confusion, which is real; the registry outranks it, which is the whole point of §6.1 'registry first'. The 1994 variant moves to the refuted set rather than becoming a second mode.
deviations_from_spec.source: Fixture openfda-k931783 (HTTP 200): date_received 1993-04-09, decision_date 1993-11-22. Confirmed against the primary record, not reported.

deviations_from_spec.this_file_says: regulatory_clearance anchored to K002489; date contested
deviations_from_spec.why: da Vinci is absent from the openFDA PMA database and has 115 records in 510(k). The PMA query path is proven working by openfda-pma-smoke (200, 56,853 records), so the NOT_FOUND is a genuine absence. The spec row states the same clearance-vs-approval error the negative case exists to catch. The date is left contested because the 510(k) search returned 25 of 115 records in unspecified order.
Same finding as da Vinci. ROBODOC is absent from PMA and has exactly two 510(k) records, so unlike da Vinci the result set is complete and the earliest date is definitive.

Refuted is strictly more severe than contested in the §6.5 ordering, so the spec's bar (must not be corroborated) is exceeded. The spec expected contested on the assumption ROBODOC held a real PMA that sources confused with AESOP's clearance; no such PMA exists, so the asserted event did not occur in any form.

precision_contract.rule: claim.date_precision and expect.date.precision must each match the granularity of their own date string. A verifier must never return a precision finer than the sources support.
precision_contract.modes_rule: expect.date.modes is a list of {value, precision}. Precision is per-mode, not per-field, because a contested date can have modes of different granularity: da Vinci's registry mode is a day (2001-03-02) while the spec's disputed mode is a month (2000-07). A single field-level precision cannot express that, and forcing one would either invent precision for the coarse mode or discard it from the fine one. expect.date.precision remains the precision of the best-supported mode.

claim.description: AESOP received FDA 510(k) clearance as an endoscope positioner.

date.note: DEVIATES FROM SPEC §8, which predicts 'contested (date bimodal)' across 1993–1994. The primary record settles it: K931783 was received 1993-04-09 and decided 1993-11-22, both within 1993. The secondary-source disagreement is real, but the registry outranks it — which is what §6.1 'registry first' is for. Day precision because the record states a day.

event_type.note: A 510(k) is a clearance, definitively (§6.1). Unaffected by the date finding, and still the counterweight to the ROBODOC 'first FDA-approved' superlative in the negative case.

conflation.note: No date conflation. The 1994 variant is not a second mode of a bimodal distribution — it is simply wrong, and is covered as a refuted case below.

date.note: K072629: received 2007-09-17, decided 2008-08-06. A cross-year record — received one year, decided the next — and still one event. §6.6 must not read this as bimodal.

event_type.note: CORRECTED from regulatory_approval. ROBODOC is absent from the openFDA PMA database and present in 510(k) with exactly two records; the PMA query is proven working by openfda-pma-smoke (56,853 records) and openfda-pma-syntax-control. It was CLEARED, never approved.

date.note: DISPUTED — see disputed[] for the unresolved part. Spec §8 says 2000-07; the earliest clearance seen is K002489, decided 2001-03-02 and RECEIVED 2000-08-10. The received date is the likeliest origin of a '2000' in secondary sources, but it is August, not July, so it does not explain 2000-07 either. Crucially the search returned only 25 of 115 records in openFDA's default unspecified order, so an earlier record may simply not have been seen. Not resolvable from current fixtures.

event_type.note: CORRECTED from regulatory_approval. da Vinci is absent from the openFDA PMA database and has 115 records in 510(k). It was CLEARED, never approved — the same clearance-vs-approval error this system exists to catch, found inside its own golden set.

conflation.note: Must NOT be conflated with the 2022 entry despite the shared acronym. If entity drift is detected across these two, it should surface on entity, not date.

conflation.note: 'Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot' (2022) and 'Smart Tissue Anastomosis Robot' (2016) are materially different systems. §6.6 acronym drift: the alias expansions differ, which is entity drift and produces false corroboration if missed.

refuted.note: The same event as aesop-510k-clearance, dated wrongly. Because both carry registry_id K931783 they derive the SAME claim id — one event with a disputed date, not two events. A verifier that treats them as separate claims will render one clearance twice on the timeline.

entity_aliases: Automated Endoscopic System for Optimal Positioning

date.note: Not merely unsupported — actively contradicted. K931783's decision date is 1993-11-22, and no part of its lifecycle falls in 1994; the received date is 1993-04-09. This is the distinction between 'refuted' and 'unverified' (§4), and the only golden entry exercising it.

event_type.note: Right about what happened, wrong about when — the §6.2 case, in its cleanest form.

conflation.note: One record, one event. Nothing has been merged; a date is simply wrong.

negative.note: REQUIRED. If this returns corroborated, verification is not working and no other feature matters (§8). REWORDED after the PMA finding: the original framing contrasted ROBODOC's supposed PMA approval against AESOP's mere clearance. That premise was wrong. ROBODOC has NO PMA record either, so the claim fails harder than the spec anticipated — the event it asserts did not occur in any form.

claim.description: ROBODOC was the first surgical robot approved by the FDA.

expect.overall_note: DEVIATES FROM SPEC §8, which requires 'contested'. Refuted is strictly more severe (§6.5 severity order: refuted > contested > unverified > single_source > corroborated), so the spec's actual bar — that this must not come back corroborated — is exceeded rather than missed. The spec expected contested because it assumed ROBODOC held a real PMA that sources confused with AESOP's clearance. There is no PMA.

event_type.note: ROBODOC is absent from the openFDA PMA database and present in 510(k) with two records. The PMA query is proven working (openfda-pma-smoke: 56,853 records), so this is absence from a database that covers the period, not absence of evidence. 'regulatory_approval' is contradicted, not merely unsupported.

date.note: 1992 is ROBODOC's first clinical use. Its only FDA clearance is 2008-08-06 (K072629). The date is attached to the wrong event AND the wrong event type.

superlative.note: §6.3: any competing claimant with sources makes this contested, full stop, regardless of how many sources back the original. Note the superlative is contested while the fields under it are refuted — a claim can be disputed among sources while being independently disprovable against the registry.

competing_claimants.note: Cleared via 510(k) in 1993, earlier than any ROBODOC FDA decision. A competing claimant for 'first', though on the correct reading neither entity was ever FDA-APPROVED.

conflation.note: REWORDED after the PMA finding. Neither device has an approval: ROBODOC and AESOP were both CLEARED via 510(k), and openFDA holds no PMA record for either. So the conflation is not one device's approval being mistaken for another's clearance — it is that the phrase 'FDA-approved' is applied across this whole field to devices that were cleared, collapsing two distinct regulatory instruments into one word. That is broader and more consequential than the spec described, and it is why regulatory_clearance and regulatory_approval are separate EventType values.

cross_year_control.note: CONFIRMED against fixture openfda-k963126-cross-year. A single record whose received and decision dates fall in different calendar years. It is one event's lifecycle, not two events, so the verifier must report decision_date and must NOT flag conflation. A discriminator firing here would fire across most of openFDA. Note this is an AESOP record too, so the same device has both a same-year record (K931783) and a cross-year one — which is precisely why the cross-year hypothesis for AESOP's disputed date was wrong: the mechanism exists in the data but does not explain the 1993/1994 split.
